telegramBot.claim: deployed source and running unit presence only; not authenticated or due-run acceptance

semantics: transactional due order insert plus schedule CAS advance

schemaDrift: resource references runs_limit but production table has no runs_limit column
resource offers paused/completed filters but table constraint allows only active/cancelled

negativeSurfaces.site: no DCA route or template in deployed Relay scope
negativeSurfaces.miniApp: no DCA string, tab or route in deployed webapp
negativeSurfaces.api: no HTTP DCA endpoint; bot calls repository directly
negativeSurfaces.native: no DCA contract or implementation in native-wallet scope

riskFindings: The runner is a money writer because it creates pending orders without a separate immutable DCA execution intent/idempotency key/audit correlation record.
Schedules have no enforced run limit and recur until cancellation.
A missing rate is coerced to zero and can create a pending order with zero agreed rate and crypto amount.
The database commit precedes Telegram delivery, so notification failure can leave a silent pending order.
The label auto-purchase overstates behavior: the runner creates a payment-required order; it does not debit the customer automatically.
blockers: no bounded non-production end-to-end due-run to payment-handoff acceptance
nextCanonicalItem: Add limit orders to the six-surface E0.4 inventory with exact repository and runtime evidence.
